title: A field finite type over a subring is finite over a principal localization which is a field
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $R\subseteq K$ be a commutative subring containing $1$. Suppose $K$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Then there exists $s\in R$, $s\ne0$, such that the principal localization $R_s=R[1/s]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], embedded in $K$ by $r/s^n\mapsto r s^{-n}$, is a field and $K$ is finite-dimensional as a vector space over $R_s$.

proof.text:
Since $R\subseteq K$ contains $1
e0$, $R$ is a domain, so $(0)$ is a prime of $R$ whose closure $V(0)$ is all of $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$: it is a generic point of $T$. Let $h:P=\operatorname{Spec}K	o T$ be the morphism induced by the inclusion [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\mathfrak q\mapsto\mathfrak q\cap R$. The only prime of $K$ is $(0)$ and $(0)\cap R=(0)$, so $P$ is one point and $h(P)=\{(0)\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] with $U=P$, $V=T$ and the finite type ring map $R	o K$, $h$ is locally of finite type; it is quasi-compact since $P$ is a single point, hence of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-closed-subset-fibre-nonempty] with $C=P$ and $\eta=(0)$: the fibre over $\eta$ contains the point of $P$, so there is an open $U
i(0)$ of $T$ with $h^{-1}(t)
e\emptyset$ for every $t\in U$, that is $(0)\in U\subseteq h(P)=\{(0)\}$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i), choose $s$ with $(0)\in D(s)\subseteq U$; thus $s\ne0$ and $D(s)=\{(0)\}$. Set $A=R_s$. The fraction formulas in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] show that $r/s^n\mapsto rs^{-n}$ is a ring homomorphism into $K$. If its value is zero, then $r=0$ in $K$ and hence in $R$, so it is injective. In particular $A$ is a nonzero domain. Part (ii) of the basic-open node identifies $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $D(s)$, so it has just the prime $(0)$.

Every nonzero $a\in A$ is a unit: otherwise $(a)$ is proper and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] places it inside a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. A maximal ideal is prime: if $bc\in\mathfrak m$ and $b\notin\mathfrak m$, write $1=u+vb$ with $u\in\mathfrak m$ and multiply by $c$ to get $c\in\mathfrak m$. Thus $\mathfrak m=(0)$ by Step 2, contradicting $0\ne a\in\mathfrak m$. Consequently $A$ is a field by [def-weil-field].

Choose finite $R$-algebra generators $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of $K$ using [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Every element of $K$ is a polynomial in them with coefficients in $R\subseteq A$, so they also generate $K$ as an $A$-algebra. Since $A$ and $K$ are fields, [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] gives $\dim_A K<\infty$. Together with the embedding of Step 2 and $s\ne0$, this proves every clause.
